input.quote: 9.3 Customer may terminate an Order Form immediately if Vendor suffers a material Security Incident, repeatedly misses a critical service level, violates Applicable Law in performing the Services, or infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
input.rationale:
Section 9 provides only for-cause exits (9.1 material breach, 9.2 insolvency, 9.3 Customer special-cause rights) and 9.5 on Order Form severability; Sections 8, 10, 11 and 27.3 add only non-renewal on 180 days' notice and a force-majeure exit. No termination-for-convenience right exists anywhere for either party, while Section 8.1 commits us to a three-year term. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under the rule, so we inserted the preferred 30 days' notice right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees. Vendor has no convenience right today, and the new clause confirms that position, so no Vendor-side concern arises.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.86

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty, early-termination charge, or further liability, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, since this three-year Agreement currently offers us no no-fault exit. If helpful, we can move to 60 days' notice.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund and confirming Vendor has none.
